30.102 Electromagnetics & Applications

Underwater Wireless Communications

Acoustic vs Optical vs RF / Magneto-Inductive

"On land, we take wireless connectivity for granted. Put that same radio 10 meters underwater, and it's dead within centimeters. Why?"
SUTD | Term 5 Presentation 1 / 7

The Core Problem: Seawater Eats RF

  • Seawater is lossy & conductive — σ ≈ 4 S/m
  • Skin depth shrinks fast with frequency: δ = √(2 / ωμσ)
  • At MHz+: penetration is centimeters, not meters
  • Decent bandwidth (MHz+) sits exactly where seawater kills the signal
  • No single dominant technology — only tradeoffs
  • This divergence is why the entire underwater comms field exists

Key insight: RF works on land because air has σ ≈ 0. The ocean is ~10⁹× more conductive.

30.102 EM & Apps | Underwater Wireless Communications2 / 7

Acoustic: Long Range, Low Rate

  • Physics — sound at c ≈ 1500 m/s, 4× faster than air; much lower attenuation than RF
  • Range — km to tens of km; up to 100s of km at very low frequency / high power
  • Bandwidth — kbps, drops with range; hard range-bandwidth tradeoff
  • Impairments — multipath from surface/seafloor → severe ISI
  • Doppler — worsened by platform motion (subs, AUVs)
  • Latency — seconds-scale round trip → ARQ breaks
  • Best for — submarine comms, ocean sensor backbone, AUV command/control

Absorption climbs steeply above ~50 kHz — bandwidth is the price paid for range.

30.102 EM & Apps | Underwater Wireless Communications3 / 7

Optical (Blue-Green): Short Range, High Rate

  • Physics — blue-green (~450–550 nm; minimum near 418 nm in pure water)
  • Range — 10s to ~100 m, depending heavily on turbidity
  • Bandwidth — Mbps to Gbps, orders of magnitude above acoustic
  • Turbidity — clear ocean vs murky coastal water: night-and-day
  • Pointing — tight alignment required; hard for anything mobile
  • Best for — AUV docking offload, ROV-to-surface HD video / sensor dumps

Reference systems: Sonardyne BlueComm (10 Mbps), WHOI optical modems, Ambalux.

30.102 EM & Apps | Underwater Wireless Communications4 / 7

RF / Magneto-Inductive: Tough Conditions, Short Range

  • Physics — near-field magnetic induction sidesteps far-field RF propagation loss
  • Range — typically under 10 m
  • Bandwidth — moderate; better than acoustic at short range, lower than optical
  • Key advantage — insensitive to turbidity and multipath
  • Tradeoff — 1/r³ coupling rolloff bounds range
  • Best for — diver-to-diver, short buoy links, turbid / reflective water

Near-field coupling rather than radiation — physics doesn't care about water clarity.

No Universal Winner — Hybrid Systems Win

Takeaways

  • Each technology occupies a different corner of the tradeoff space
  • Real systems increasingly hybridize modalities
  • AUV example: acoustic for long-range C2, optical for high-rate bursts at the dock
  • Match the technology to the mission, not the other way around
"The ocean forces you to pick your poison — the real engineering question is knowing which poison fits your mission."
